summary:
It was really wonderful to talk to you on the telephone. I’d like to send you a book of mine to read until the new one comes out in February, but anyhow here is an early story of mine which I think a lot of—it was my first really good sale, and is just now back in print. Oddly, the Russians liked it, too; so much so that they published it in their leading magazine, Ogonek, (their circulation was a million and a half copies, and the unusual fact that they’d be printing a story by a U.S. writer got mentioned on the radio here in the U.S. They even paid me, 
too, and illustrated the story with many pictures.) They mailed me a copy of Ogonek with my story in it, but the U.S. Postal Authorities destroyed it on the grounds that it was “Communist Propaganda.” My own story. It is a story I’ve always liked, because of the anti-war theme and what it does to children to be subjected to the artificial warscare sensational sales-pitches that big business drums up to sell products. But more fundamentally it has what I think is a uni­ versal theme: the fact that parents really do not listen to nor pay any attention to the fears and needs of their own children. 

Also I’m enclosing the jacket for my forthcoming Doubleday novel, FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID, mainly because it has a picture of me on the back cover taken recently, so you can see how serious-looking I’ve become. I think it’s a well-designed jacket and goes good with the book when it does come off the presses. And later I’ll...
